Quick triage summary (11:00 PST):
- Ingested Emberlane traces and logs. Confirmed increased 500s hit rate on /v1/checkout/generate-call (model routing layer).
- Root cause hypothesis: transient KV cache eviction combined with autoscaler decisions that triggered a mix of quantized and fp16 kernels; this caused higher tail latency under the retry flood.
- Impact window: 08:28–09:12 PST, peak error rate 7.3% at 08:42.
- Short-term mitigations applied (08:50): pinned model variant to fp16 for the leaflet-serving pool, disabled aggressive autoscale down for the next 6 hours, and enabled a temporary per-customer token-bucket to smooth retries.

Attaching: emberlane-logs-20261104.zip (logs + traces).

Next steps we’re working now:
1) Full KV cache investigation and whether TTL config changed on your side; Jonas is on it.
2) Quantization profile review — if we misrouted a quantized variant under heavy tail; Kim will validate.
3) Stitch an RCA draft and short-term action list for the Nov 5 readout.

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Claire / team — quick technical note from cache analysis:
- We observed a KV cache thrash pattern coinciding with a rollout that began 07:55 PST (your side indicated a small traffic shift to new cart variant at 07:50 — thanks).
- Cache miss amplification + retries produced uneven sequence length distributions; our routing logic incorrectly selected a quantized variant for several long sequences, increasing decode time on those shards.
- No persistent data corruption; this was a latency-regression coupling (customer rollout + autoscaler behavior).

Immediate recomendation: pin the Emberlane account to the stable model variant until we complete a quantization profile re-eval (ETA 48 hours). We also recommend temporary retry-backoff on Emberlane side for client retries during this window.

-Jonas
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
